section.objects.intro: Answers may gain new fields in future versions — skip unknown fields quietly. Ids are strings (UUIDs), time is Unix seconds.
section.methods.intro: Required parameters are in bold. Every method returns its value in `result` inside `{"ok":true,…}`. Every method also works with `GET` (parameters in the query string); from a form or the query string numbers and flags may be strings (`limit=50`, `disable_notification=true`), arrays and objects are JSON strings.
section.events.intro: A bot's event journal keeps events for **24 hours**, at most **1000** (a "Read all messages" bot — 10 000; the oldest go first, the count of dropped ones is `dropped_update_count`). Acknowledged events (`offset`, `ack`, a `2xx` answer from your URL) are deleted. Every event is an [Update](#update): `update_id` plus exactly one of these fields.
section.events.notes: A bot does not see its own actions as events: sending, editing and deleting through the Bot API produce no events for the bot (the exception is `voice_state` — the bot learns about its own joins and leaves). Pins, "typing", read receipts, polls and stickers are not delivered to bots.
object.*.instance_domain: present for guests from other instances (federation); usernames may collide with local ones — authorize by `id`
object.*.dropped_update_count: how many events the journal limit dropped (present if any)
object.*.server_muted: a moderator muted it on the server
object.Attachment: A file attached to a message.
object.Attachment.url: a link made **for your bot**, downloaded with a plain `GET` without headers; do not publish it. It works while the bot has access to the conversation
object.BotCommand: A command in the hint list shown when a person types `/`, e.g. `{ "command": "status", "description": "Server state" }`.
object.BotCommandScope.type: `default`, `all_private_chats` (DMs) or `all_group_chats` (servers). Other types → `400`. DMs use `all_private_chats` if set, otherwise `default`; servers use `all_group_chats`, otherwise `default`
object.BotUser: The bot itself (the `getMe` result): a [User](#user) plus the bot's profile and what the server can do. Check `features` instead of guessing by version; an older server does not send `api_version`/`features`.
object.BotUser.public: whether everyone may message the bot
object.BotUser.api_version: server Bot API version: 2 — buttons and commands, 3 — servers, 4 — voice
object.BotUser.features: what the server supports: `polling`, `ws`, `webhook`, `keyboards`, `commands`, `client_id`, `servers`, `reactions`, `parse_mode`, `webhook_batch`, `voice`, …; new ones are appended
object.CallbackQuery: A button with `callback_data` was pressed. Answer it with `answerCallbackQuery`.
object.CallbackQuery.message: the message with the buttons, whole (including `reply_markup`)
object.Chat: A conversation. 🔴 **Check `type`**: code that assumed `"dm"` will see other values; ignore unknown ones.
object.Chat.id: conversation id — the value to pass as `chat_id`
object.Chat.type: `dm` — 1:1 chat, `channel` — text channel of a server, `server` — the server itself (membership events and `getChat` only), `voice` — voice channel (voice methods only)
object.Chat.title: for channels and servers: the name
object.ChatFullInfo.title: for channels and servers: the name
object.ChatFullInfo.user: in a DM: the other participant
object.ChatFullInfo.member_count: for a server: number of members
object.ChatMember: A server member (`getChatMember`, `getChatMembers`). Permissions are not flags as in Telegram: look up the roles with `getServer`.
object.ChatMember.nickname: nickname on this server (present if set)
object.ChatMemberUpdated.from: who changed it (the person, or a server admin)
object.ChatMembersPage.next_offset: pass it as `offset` for the next page; absent on the last page
object.Error: An error answer; the HTTP status equals `error_code`. Branch on `error_code`, not on the text of `description`.
object.Error.retry_after: only on `429`: whole seconds to wait (also the `Retry-After` header)
object.InlineKeyboardButton: A button under a message: `text` plus **exactly one** of `callback_data` and `url`. Other Telegram button kinds (`web_app`, `switch_inline_query`, `login_url`, …) are ignored.
object.InlineKeyboardButton.callback_dat: up to **64 bytes** UTF-8, not characters (Cyrillic is 2 bytes per letter: 32 letters). Pressing sends the bot a `callback_query` with this string
object.InlineKeyboardButton.url: `http(s)` only, no `user:password@` in the address. The person is asked "Open link?" for foreign addresses
object.InlineKeyboardMarkup: Buttons under a message: rows of buttons, at least one row, 1–8 buttons in a row, at most 100 in total. From a form or the query string — a JSON string.
object.InputEmbed: A card for `sendMessage` (`embeds`), the same format as incoming webhooks. Card images only from this instance's storage or an uploaded file (`attachment://<file name>`, servers only); an external image is shown as a link.
object.InputEmbed.title: title
object.InputEmbed.timestamp: ISO 8601 time shown at the bottom
object.InputEmbed.fields: up to 25 fields `{ name, value, inline? }`
object.InputEmbed.author: `{ name, url?, icon_url? }`
object.Message.edit_date: present only if the message was edited
object.Message.text: text (may be empty if the message has only an attachment or a card)
object.Message.reply_to_message_id: present if it is a reply
object.Message.reply_markup: present if the message has buttons
object.MessageDeleted: A message disappeared for the bot.
object.MessageEmbed: A card as stored by the server (field names as in the message feed: `iconUrl`, `imageLink`).
object.MessageEmbed.title: title
object.MessageEmbed.author: author line
object.MessageEmbed.image: big picture from this instance's storage
object.MessageEmbed.thumbnail: small picture from this instance's storage
object.MessageEmbed.imageLink: an external `image` — shown as a link, not loaded
object.MessageEmbed.thumbnailLink: an external `thumbnail` — shown as a link, not loaded
object.MessageReactionUpdated: A person changed their reactions to a message (`message_reaction`).
object.ServerBrief: A server the bot is on (`getMyServers`).
object.ServerBrief.title: name
object.ServerInfo: A server as the bot sees it (`getServer`).
object.ServerInfo.title: name
object.ServerInfo.channels: channels the bot can see; `can_send` — whether the bot may post there
object.ServerInfo.roles: roles; `managed` — a bot role (cannot be given to anyone else)
object.ServerMemberUpdated: Someone joined, left, was kicked, banned or unbanned on a server (`chat_member`).
object.ServerMemberUpdated.from: who did it (the member themselves or a moderator)
object.Update: An event: `update_id` plus **exactly one** content field (see [Events](#events)). If a field that is not listed arrives (in future versions), skip it quietly.
object.Update.update_id: increasing but **not necessarily consecutive** (the counter is shared by the whole instance)
object.Update.voice_state: someone joined or left a voice channel
object.VoiceChatMember: Who is in a voice channel now (`getVoiceChatMembers`).
object.VoiceJoinResult: Where and how to connect to voice (`joinVoice`).
object.VoiceJoinResult.token: LiveKit token; LiveKit refreshes it while the session is alive, after a full drop call `joinVoice` again
object.VoiceJoinResult.server_muted: the bot is muted by a moderator
object.VoiceJoinResult.audio: what to publish: PCM `sample_rate` 48000, `channels` 2, `bitrate` as requested
object.VoiceStateUpdated: Someone joined or left a voice channel of the server (`voice_state`).
object.VoiceStateUpdated.move_to: only to the bot itself, when a moderator moved it: join this channel (the SDK does it on its own)
object.WebhookInfo.url: the URL; an empty string if none
object.WebhookInfo.pending_update_count: how many events are waiting in the journal
object.WebhookInfo.last_error_date: time of the last failure (present if there was one)
object.WebhookInfo.last_error_message: the last failure, a short English text, e.g. `Wrong response from the webhook: HTTP 502`
object.WebhookInfo.disabled_date: present if the server switched delivery off after a series of failures
param.*.parse_mode: omitted — our markup; `HTML` — a Telegram subset converted to our markup; `MarkdownV2` → `400`
method.getMe.summary: Who am I. Handy to check that the token works.
method.getUpdates.notes: Events come by ascending `update_id`. Until acknowledged with `offset`, the same events arrive again (this is how bot restarts are survived). If a delivery URL is set — `409`.

**One consumer at a time** (as in Telegram): a new `getUpdates` or WebSocket of the same bot **replaces** the previous one — a waiting `getUpdates` answers `409 Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates request; make sure that only one bot instance is running`, an open WebSocket is closed with `4009`. Two copies of the bot with one token knock each other out — stop one. Reissuing the token, disabling the bot or all bots also ends a waiting `getUpdates` at once (`401`/`403`) instead of handing it a batch.
Do not poll with two processes of the same bot: both will see the same events and answer twice.
param.getUpdates.offset: acknowledge all events with `update_id` **lower** than `offset` (they are deleted) and return from `offset` on. Normally the last `update_id` + 1. Unset or ≤ 0 returns everything not yet acknowledged
param.getUpdates.timeout: seconds, default 0 (answer at once). Above 0 the server waits up to `timeout` seconds for the first event (long polling)
param.getUpdates.allowed_updates: only these kinds, e.g. `["message","callback_query"]`. The rest stay in the journal until acknowledged by `offset`. Unknown kinds are **ignored** (not a `400`): a bot written for a newer server keeps working
method.setWebhook.summary: Turn on event delivery to a URL (see [Delivery to a URL](#delivery-to-a-url)).
method.setWebhook.notes: The URL is checked immediately (see [SSRF protection](#ssrf-protection)); an error is `400 Bad Request: bad webhook: …`. After the call `getUpdates` answers `409` and open WebSockets are closed with code `4009`. Calling `setWebhook` again with a new URL or secret resets the failure counter.
param.setWebhook.url: `https://…`, no login or password in the URL
param.setWebhook.secret_token: **required**: every delivery is signed with it
param.setWebhook.batch: batched delivery: the POST body is an array of up to 100 updates, signed as a whole; a `2xx` confirms the whole batch
method.deleteWebhook.summary: Turn delivery to a URL off; returns the bot to `getUpdates`/WebSocket.
method.sendMessage.notes: At least one of `text`, `embeds` or a file is required (buttons alone are not enough). If `text` is empty and there are cards, `Message.text` is an empty string.
Errors: `400` (empty, not your chat, reply target missing), `403` (bot blocked by the person / account deleted / no right to post in the channel), `415` (SVG/HTML), `429`, `503` (no file storage).
param.sendMessage.chat_id: a DM or text channel the bot is in
param.sendMessage.text: the same markup as people's messages
param.sendMessage.client_id: your own id of this send: repeating `sendMessage` with the same `client_id` (a network drop, a restart) returns **the same** message instead of a second one. The same `client_id` with a different chat or content → `400`. Ignored in channels for now
param.sendMessage.files[0]: files `files[0]`…`files[9]`: up to **10**, each up to **25 MB**. Other fields are strings; `embeds` and `reply_markup` — JSON strings
method.editMessageText.summary: Change the text of the bot's own message.
method.editMessageText.notes: The result has `edit_date`. Only the bot's **own** messages can be edited, otherwise `400`. The person sees an ordinary edit.
param.editMessageText.reply_markup: buttons after the edit. 🔴 **Omitted — the buttons are removed** (as in Telegram)
method.deleteMessage.notes: In a 1:1 conversation a bot, like a person, can delete both its own messages and the other person's — **for both**; in a channel — as the bot's role permits. Deleting the same message again also returns `true`.
method.sendChatAction.summary: Show "typing…" to the other side. Call it before a long operation.
method.getChat.summary: Details of a conversation, channel or server.
method.editMessageReplyMarkup.summary: Change only the buttons of the bot's own message.
method.editMessageReplyMarkup.notes: The person does **not** see "(edited)". The same buttons again are not an error (Telegram answers `400 message is not modified`; we just return the message).
method.answerCallbackQuery.notes: Answer **once** and within **15 seconds**: the person's client waits that long, then shows "the bot did not answer". A press lives **25 seconds**: until then the answer is accepted (a slightly late one too) and the event is delivered; after that it is neither. A second answer, a late one or someone else's id → `400 query is too old and response timeout expired or query id is invalid` (Telegram's text). Telegram's `url` and `cache_time` are not supported yet.
param.answerCallbackQuery.text: a toast for the person; without it the "clock" on the button just goes out
param.answerCallbackQuery.show_alert: a dialog with an "OK" button instead of a toast
method.setMyCommands.notes: The list is the hint shown when a person types `/` (and the "/" button next to the message box). Commands still arrive as ordinary `message` with text `/status …` — parse them yourself.
param.setMyCommands.commands: **replaces** the whole list; `[]` — remove. A repeated name → `400`
method.deleteMyCommands.summary: Remove the command list (the same as `setMyCommands` with `[]`).
method.setMessageReaction.summary: Set the bot's reactions to a message (in DMs too); the set is replaced, `[]` — remove.
method.pinChatMessage.summary: Pin a message in a channel (needs "Manage messages").
method.unpinChatMessage.summary: Unpin a message in a channel (needs "Manage messages").
method.getChatHistory.summary: Earlier messages of a channel: the latest page before `before_message_id` (or the newest), oldest first; polls and stickers are skipped. Only for "Read all messages" bots with "Read history" in the channel.
param.getChatHistory.before_message_id: messages older than this one; omitted — from the newest
param.getChatMember.chat_id: a server or a channel of it
method.getChatMemberCount.summary: How many members a server has.
param.getChatMemberCount.chat_id: a server or a channel of it
param.getChatMembers.chat_id: a server or a channel of it
param.getChatMembers.offset: `next_offset` of the previous page; omitted — the first page
method.getServer.summary: A server: the channels the bot can see (with `can_send`) and roles (with `managed`).
method.addChatMemberRole.summary: Give a role to a member (needs "Manage roles"; the role must be below the bot's).
param.addChatMemberRole.chat_id: a server or a channel of it
method.removeChatMemberRole.summary: Take a role from a member (needs "Manage roles"; the role must be below the bot's).
param.removeChatMemberRole.chat_id: a server or a channel of it
method.banChatMember.summary: Ban a member (needs the matching permission; the target must be below the bot).
param.banChatMember.chat_id: a server or a channel of it
method.unbanChatMember.summary: Lift a ban (needs the matching permission).
param.unbanChatMember.chat_id: a server or a channel of it
method.kickChatMember.summary: Kick a member from the server (needs the matching permission; the target must be below the bot).
param.kickChatMember.chat_id: a server or a channel of it
method.leaveChat.summary: The bot leaves a server; its role goes with it.
param.leaveChat.chat_id: a server or a channel of it
method.joinVoice.summary: Join a voice channel to play audio (see [Voice](#voice-api-4)). The bot never hears people.
method.joinVoice.notes: Connect to LiveKit at `url` with `token` and publish PCM 48 kHz stereo as a `MICROPHONE` track. One voice channel per server: joining another channel of the same server moves the bot. Errors, in this order: `403 voice is disabled for bots on this server`, `400 chat not found`, `400 chat is a server; use a channel id`, `400 chat is not a voice channel`, `403 not enough rights to connect to the voice chat`, `403 not enough rights to speak in the voice chat`, `429`, `400 too many bots in the voice chat`, `400 too many active voice chats`.
method.leaveVoice.summary: Leave a voice channel, or all of them. Idempotent: always `true`.
param.leaveVoice.chat_id: voice channel id; omitted — leave all
method.getVoiceChatMembers.summary: Who is in a voice channel now.
event.message: a person wrote to the bot in a DM, or a message the bot may see arrived in a channel (see [Bots on servers](#bots-on-servers-api-3))
event.edited_message: such a message was edited (in channels filtered by the new text)
event.message_deleted: a message disappeared for the bot (deleted for both in a DM; in channels — to "read all" bots and the author)
event.my_chat_member: in a DM: a person opened the conversation (`new_status: "member"`; also when they press "Message" again after deleting the chat), deleted it on their side (`"left"`), blocked the bot (`"kicked"`) or unblocked it; on a server (`chat.type: "server"`): the bot was added, removed or banned
event.callback_query: a person pressed a button with `callback_data` under the bot's message. **Not delivered if older than 25 seconds**
event.message_reaction: a person changed reactions (to read-all bots and the message author; in DMs — to any message of the chat)
event.chat_member: someone joined, left, was kicked, banned or unbanned on a server the bot is on
event.voice_state: someone joined or left a voice channel the bot can see (including the bot itself — so it learns it was disconnected)
